papers.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative, Multi-Agent Games
papers.authors_short: Yu, Velu, Vinitsky, Gao, Wang, Bayen, Wu
papers.api_title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative, Multi-Agent Games
papers.core_idea: PPO with decentralised actors and a centralised value function (global-state input) matches or beats off-policy MARL on MPE, SMAC, GRF and Hanabi. Performance hinges on value normalisation, critic input design, few epochs, no minibatch splitting, clip below 0.2 and large batches.
papers.what_to_take: Use its five suggestions as the fixed recipe for the MAPPO arm. SMAT's 20 epochs and 4 minibatches depart from Suggestion 3 (at most 10 epochs on hard tasks, no splitting); equalise epochs across arms.
papers.left_untested: Heterogeneous, physically coupled agents (26 muscle excitations vs 2 hip torques), staged or frozen-actor schedules, and generalisation to unseen partners; benchmarks are games, mostly homogeneous agents with parameter sharing.
papers.feasibility_notes: No extra simulation: same rollouts as the shared-critic arm; only critic inputs, value normalisation and per-agent value heads change.

papers.title: Trust Region Policy Optimisation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors_short: Kuba, Chen, Wen, Wen, Sun, Wang, Yang
papers.api_title: Trust Region Policy Optimisation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Multi-agent advantage decomposition lemma plus a sequential update scheme: agents update one at a time in a random permutation, each weighting its advantage by the already-updated agents' new/old policy ratios, giving monotonic joint improvement without parameter sharing (HATRPO, HAPPO).
papers.what_to_take: HAPPO is the principled sequential-schedule arm: fixed human-then-exo vs exo-then-human vs random order at equal budget. Its ratio-weighted advantage shows how a shared critic's advantage should change after the partner updates.
papers.left_untested: Stage-length freezing (millions of steps), agents with very different action size and plasticity, and whether update order changes which joint equilibrium is reached; ACPO (2606.30072) argues alternating updates can stall at suboptimal Nash equilibria.
papers.feasibility_notes: Two agents add one ratio product per minibatch; negligible cost. PKU-MARL/HARL (PyTorch) is the maintained implementation to port into the MyoAssist PPO loop.

papers.title: Dealing With Non-stationarity in Decentralized Cooperative Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning via Multi-Timescale Learning
papers.authors_short: Nekoei, Badrinaaraayanan, Sinha, Amini, Rajendran, Mahajan, Chandar
papers.api_title: Dealing With Non-stationarity in Decentralized Cooperative Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning via Multi-Timescale Learning
papers.core_idea: Independent (simultaneous) learning need not converge; sequential learning, where one agent updates while the others are frozen, converges to an agent-by-agent optimum but is slow. Multi-timescale learning rotates one fast learner while others learn slowly; MTPPO matches or beats IPPO on 12 EPyMARL tasks.
papers.what_to_take: Its parameterisation spans the schedule space: slow rate 0 is SMAT Stage 3, equal rates is Stage 4. Sweep rate ratio and switching period at fixed reward and torque to isolate schedule from curricula.
papers.left_untested: Continuous musculoskeletal control, agents of very unequal size and plasticity, a shared critic (it uses per-agent critics), and schedules coupled to curricula; only discrete-action EPyMARL benchmarks were tested.
papers.feasibility_notes: Two learning rates and a switching period: a few config lines on the two-actor PPO. Cheap to sweep at proxy budgets, 5+ seeds.

papers.title: On Centralized Critics in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.api_title: On Centralized Critics in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Formal and empirical analysis of centralised vs decentralised critics in CTDE actor-critic: critic centralisation is not strictly beneficial, and state-based critics can introduce bias and variance relative to history-based critics when actors observe only part of the state.
papers.what_to_take: Treat critic input as a sweep axis: SMAT's exo actor sees only an 18-D hip window and the critic inputs are unspecified. Compare state, history and state+history critics before crediting the 'shared critic'.
papers.left_untested: Physically coupled continuous control where one critic serves two actors with very different observations and action sizes, and effects on partner transfer; experiments use small cooperative benchmarks (Dec-Tiger, particle, SMAC).
papers.feasibility_notes: Critic variants change only the critic network input; each is one extra arm at proxy budget. Author code shows the input constructions.

papers.title: "Other-Play" for Zero-Shot Coordination
papers.core_idea: Self-play converges on arbitrary conventions that fail with independently trained partners. Other-Play trains under random relabelling by known environment symmetries, yielding convention-free policies; evaluated by cross-play matrices of independently trained agents in Hanabi and preliminarily with humans.
papers.what_to_take: Adopt cross-play as the partner-transfer test: an exo-seed by human-seed matrix, off-diagonal vs diagonal benefit. Left-right mirror symmetry of gait is a candidate symmetry group for a bilateral hip exoskeleton.
papers.left_untested: Continuous control with asymmetric roles (human vs device) and approximate rather than exact symmetries; whether physically coupled dynamics produce arbitrary conventions at all (e.g., exo torque timing tuned to one gait).
papers.feasibility_notes: Evaluation-only once policies exist; the cost is training independent humans (about 480M transitions each at SMAT Stages 1-2 scale).

papers.title: Assistax: A Multi-Agent Hardware-Accelerated Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Assistive Robotics
papers.authors_short: Hinckeldey, Fosong, Rubavicius, Miller, McInroe, Zhang, Wollstadt, Albrecht, Ramamoorthy
papers.api_title: Assistax: A Multi-Agent Hardware-Accelerated Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Assistive Robotics
papers.core_idea: JAX/MuJoCo-MJX assistive tasks where a torque-controlled robot and a simulated humanoid are co-trained with MARL (IPPO, MAPPO, MASAC; no parameter sharing), plus an ad hoc teamwork pipeline: 630 pre-trained humanoids per task varying conventions, preferences and disabilities.
papers.what_to_take: Copy its protocol: train the robot with few partners (5), test on withheld ones (625), release the partner zoo. Its coordination gap narrows when train and test partners overlap, so report overlap.
papers.left_untested: Muscle-driven humans and locomotion (its Brax humanoid acts through a few torque-controlled arm joints) and staged co-training; its held-out evaluation trains robots against frozen pre-trained humanoids, not co-adapted ones.
papers.feasibility_notes: One GPU: IPPO 40M steps in about 20 min (1024 envs, A100). Partner zoo on Hugging Face; a cheap sandbox to debug cross-play tooling.

papers.title: Is Independent Learning All You Need in the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge?
papers.authors_short: de Witt, Gupta, Makoviichuk, Makoviychuk, Torr, Sun, Whiteson
papers.api_title: Is Independent Learning All You Need in the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge?
papers.core_idea: Independent PPO, each agent learning only its own local value function, matches or beats state-of-the-art joint-learning methods on SMAC with little tuning; variant comparisons suggest its strength comes partly from robustness to some forms of environment non-stationarity.
papers.what_to_take: Include IPPO (separate human and exo critics, simultaneous updates) as the control arm: if the shared critic cannot beat it at matched transitions, the 'shared critic' is not the mechanism.
papers.left_untested: Physically coupled heterogeneous agents with a shared assistance reward, muscle actuation, staged schedules and partner transfer; SMAC is a discrete-action game.
papers.feasibility_notes: Cheapest arm: two critics instead of one, same rollouts. EPyMARL has a reference IPPO; port the logic, not the code.

papers.title: Collaborating with Humans without Human Data
papers.api_title: Collaborating with Humans without Human Data
papers.core_idea: Fictitious Co-Play trains an agent as best response to a frozen population of self-play partners plus their past checkpoints, supplying skill and convention diversity; in Overcooked it beats self-play, population play and behaviour-cloning play with novel agents and humans.
papers.what_to_take: SMAT already produces checkpoints (Stage 1-2 humans at different skill levels, across seeds). Training the exo against that frozen population is the obvious remedy arm if cross-play shows poor transfer.
papers.left_untested: Continuous physical coupling where partners differ in dynamics, not only conventions; whether early-checkpoint (unskilled) humans help or harm an assistive controller; joint fine-tuning after population training.
papers.feasibility_notes: Checkpoints are free by-products; one exo run per population. Evaluation still needs held-out humans outside the population.

papers.title: On the Utility of Learning about Humans for Human-AI Coordination
papers.authors_short: Carroll, Shah, Ho, Griffiths, Seshia, Abbeel, Dragan
papers.api_title: On the Utility of Learning about Humans for Human-AI Coordination
papers.core_idea: In Overcooked-AI, agents trained by self-play or population-based training coordinate well with themselves but poorly with a held-out proxy human (behaviour cloning on separate data); agents trained with a human model do better; a user study shows the same pattern, less strongly.
papers.what_to_take: Separate the training partner from the evaluation proxy: a human fitted to different data or trained independently is the minimum honest partner-transfer test for the exo.
papers.left_untested: Continuous biomechanical coupling where the device changes the partner's dynamics, and partner models that adapt to the device (the behaviour-cloned proxy is non-adaptive).
papers.feasibility_notes: For SMAT the proxy is an independently trained or data-imitating human, costing one Stage 1-2 run each.

papers.title: Human adaptation to adaptive machines converges to game-theoretic equilibria
papers.api_title: Human adaptation to adaptive machines converges to game-theoretic equilibria
papers.core_idea: Three human-subject experiments (n=20 each) in quadratic-cost games: the machine's adaptation rule and rate selected the co-adaptation outcome, Nash at slow gradient-descent rates, human-led Stackelberg at fast rates, and conjectural or machine-optimal equilibria with policy-space learners.
papers.what_to_take: Frame staged vs simultaneous training as equilibrium selection. Changing rates in simultaneous gradient play does not move stationary points (their note), so test whether SMAT staging changes the endpoint or only the path.
papers.left_untested: Deep RL learners on both sides, physical coupling and locomotion; humans chose scalar actions in quadratic-cost games through a browser, with general-sum costs rather than a shared assistance reward.
papers.feasibility_notes: No compute; motivates a cheap test: vary the exo-to-human learning-rate ratio in simultaneous training and check whether the endpoint moves.

papers.title: ACPO: Agent-Chained Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors_short: Matsunaga, Na, Guntara, Sanner, Poupart, Lee, Kim
papers.api_title: ACPO: Agent-Chained Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Shows the joint policy gradient decomposes exactly into per-agent terms built from per-agent score functions and decentralised critics, so independent actor updates form one joint-gradient step. Argues MAPPO-style independent and HAPPO-style alternating updates can stall at suboptimal Nash equilibria.
papers.what_to_take: Its matrix-game example, where the equilibrium MAPPO or HAPPO reach depends on initialisation, suggests SMAT's pre-trained human may decide the outcome. Test staging against 'simultaneous from the Stage-2 human'.
papers.left_untested: Two heterogeneous, physically coupled agents with musculoskeletal dynamics and staged curricula; evaluated on warehouse, SMACv2 and MA-MuJoCo, with gains growing with agent count, so the two-agent benefit may be small.
papers.feasibility_notes: No code found; per-agent critics and chained updates for two agents are a moderate PyTorch change. Treat as an optional arm.

papers.title: Human Machine Co-adaption Interface via Cooperation Markov Decision Process System
papers.authors_short: Guo, Cheng, Li, Li, Duffield, Su
papers.venue: arXiv preprint (final retitled version: Knowledge-Based Systems 291:111572, 2024, doi 10.1016/j.knosys.2024.111572)
papers.api_title: Human Machine Co-adaption Interface via Cooperation Markov Decision Process System
papers.core_idea: Models robot-assisted rehabilitation as a cooperative two-agent MDP (patient and robot) at a high abstraction layer and proposes procedures that gate each agent's policy improvement on instantaneous or accumulated value gains to curb co-adaptation non-stationarity; validated only on a numerical example.
papers.what_to_take: A value-gated switching rule (switch which actor learns when its improvement stalls) is a cheap adaptive-schedule arm to set beside fixed SMAT stage lengths.
papers.left_untested: Function approximation, PPO, continuous musculoskeletal control and real wearers; it uses finite tabular MDPs with known models. The KBS version's large-scale result remains unverified (KB reading 05).
papers.feasibility_notes: Scheduler logic only: track per-actor value improvement across PPO iterations and toggle learning flags; negligible compute.

papers.title: Human-Robotic Prosthesis as Collaborating Agents for Symmetrical Walking
papers.authors_short: Wu, Zhong, Wallace, Gao, Huang, Si
papers.api_title: Human-Robotic Prosthesis as Collaborating Agents for Symmetrical Walking
papers.core_idea: Collaborative MARL for a human and a robotic knee prosthesis: separate human and robot actors with one critic learned on the shared cost (not local costs, since they are physically coupled), tuning phase-wise impedance in OpenSim walking; beats single-agent, tailored MADDPG and COMA baselines.
papers.what_to_take: Prior art for SMAT's core design (two actors, one critic on a shared cost, physical coupling). Its with/without-human-influence ablation is a template for isolating what the second learner contributes.
papers.left_untested: Muscle-level human control, deep PPO, staged schedules and held-out users: networks have 6 hidden units, the robot sets 12 impedance parameters per gait cycle, and all evaluation is simulated with injected sensor noise.
papers.feasibility_notes: Conceptual precedent; the tiny networks and OpenSim setup are not reusable. No code link found.

papers.title: Is Inter-Seed Cross-Play Enough? Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Coordination Algorithms to Implementation Details
papers.api_title: Is Inter-Seed Cross-Play Enough? Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Coordination Algorithms to Implementation Details
papers.core_idea: Introduces cross-implementation cross-play: partners trained with varied PPO details (GAE lambda, schedules, clipping, initialisation, depth, minibatches, discount, GRU/LSTM/MLP). For Other-Play in the Yokai environment, cross-implementation scores matched within-implementation inter-seed cross-play.
papers.what_to_take: Build held-out humans by varying implementation details as well as seeds, and train at least 8 seeds per implementation because score distributions were multimodal.
papers.left_untested: Continuous physical control, algorithms other than Other-Play, and asymmetric human-device roles; one discrete benchmark (Yokai) only.
papers.feasibility_notes: Eight human seeds per implementation is unaffordable at SMAT's CPU cost; needs GPU physics or proxy-budget humans.

papers.title: Human Machine Co-Adaptation Model and Its Convergence Analysis
papers.api_title: Human Machine Co-Adaptation Model and Its Convergence Analysis
papers.core_idea: Gives sufficient conditions under which cooperative adaptive MDPs (finite, factored human, robot and shared states) converge to a unique Nash equilibrium, and adjusts value evaluation and policy improvement to favour the best (minimal-cost) equilibrium when several exist; numerical examples only.
papers.what_to_take: Vocabulary and conditions for arguing why staged and simultaneous schedules could land on different joint policies; read with Chasnov et al. and ACPO when interpreting SMAT ablations.
papers.left_untested: Function approximation, stochastic policy gradients, continuous control and any wearer; transition and reward matrices are assumed known (KB reading 06).

papers.title: Simulation study of exoskeleton–musculoskeletal coupling for exoskeleton assistance via multi-agent reinforcement learning
papers.api_title: Simulation study of exoskeleton–musculoskeletal coupling for exoskeleton assistance via multi-agent reinforcement learning
papers.core_idea: Models a 7-DOF OpenSim lower-limb musculoskeletal model and a hip exoskeleton as heterogeneous agents trained with MATD3 under centralised training and decentralised execution, using gait-data kinematic priors and a multi-objective reward; reports symmetric tracking and lower iliopsoas force and GRF peaks at three speeds.
papers.what_to_take: Occupied-claim check: 'human and hip exo as two MARL agents with a centralised critic in musculoskeletal simulation' was published in July 2026. Cite it; novelty must come from mechanism isolation and partner transfer.
papers.left_untested: The abstract reports no staged schedule, matched-budget baselines, held-out human policies or hardware test (full text paywalled, not read).
papers.feasibility_notes: Not reusable (OpenSim, off-policy MATD3, no code seen); read the full text only for its reward terms.

cluster_lessons: Treat the actor-update schedule as a continuous knob, not a staged-vs-simultaneous switch. Multi-timescale learning (Nekoei et al., 2302.02792) contains simultaneous updates (equal rates), sequential updates (slow rate 0, i.e. SMAT Stage 3) and fixed two-timescale learning as special cases, and HAPPO (2109.11251) adds a principled sequential order. Sweeping these at fixed reward weights and torque scale is the cleanest way to separate schedule from curricula.

A staged-vs-simultaneous difference may come from equilibrium selection or initialisation rather than better optimisation. ACPO (2606.30072) shows MAPPO-style and HAPPO-style updates can settle in suboptimal Nash equilibria depending on initialisation. Chasnov et al. (Sci Rep 2025) found that a machine's adaptation rule and rate moved real human-machine pairs between Nash and Stackelberg outcomes, and Su & Guo (2503.07319) formalise multiple equilibria. UniExo (2609.19690, the SMAT authors) replaced the frozen-human RL stage with supervised exo initialisation from the human's hip moments followed by joint shared-critic PPO. 'Simultaneous from the Stage-2 human' and 'supervised exo initialisation + simultaneous' are therefore mandatory controls.

Critic design is an unspecified axis, not a detail. MAPPO lists value normalisation and critic input among five factors critical to PPO performance. Lyu et al. (JAIR 2023) show critic centralisation is not strictly beneficial and that state-based critics can add bias and variance for partially observing actors. SMAT's exo actor sees only an 18-D hip window, so compare critic inputs before attributing gains to 'sharing'.

PPO settings interact with partner non-stationarity. MAPPO recommends at most 10 epochs on hard tasks, no minibatch splitting and a clip below 0.2, while SMAT uses 20 epochs, 4 minibatches and a clip of 0.15. IPPO's (2011.09533) strength was linked to robustness to some non-stationarity, and trust-region bounds for decentralised PPO (Sun et al., AAMAS 2023, 2202.00082) justify bounding per-agent ratios by agent count. Hold these equal across arms or sweep them explicitly.

Co-trained partners overfit to each other, and the co-training score hides it. Self-play agents failed with a held-out proxy human (Carroll 2019), and independently trained agents fail in cross-play without symmetry-aware training (Other-Play 2020). Assistax found a coordination gap on 625 withheld humanoids that narrows only when train and test partners overlap. In simulation SMAT evaluates its exo only with its co-trained human; its offline replay on recorded gait tests input generalisation, not closed-loop partner transfer.

Vary held-out humans along several axes, not only seeds. The axes are implementation details (inter-seed cross-play was an adequate proxy for Other-Play in 2608.03644, with 8 or more seeds per implementation), reward shaping and preferences (Assistax preferences; ZSC with diverse reward shapings, 2604.25076) and impairments (Clegg et al. 1909.06682 co-trained human and robot dressing policies per impairment; the SMAT authors' unilateral-weakness models, 2602.18862). Each independent human costs a Stage 1-2 run (about 480M transitions at SMAT scale), so the partner-transfer test depends on GPU physics or validated proxy budgets.

Treating a human and a device as two learning agents with a shared or centralised critic is an occupied framing. Wu et al. (NeurIPS 2022, prosthesis, one critic on a shared cost), Sun et al. (MBEC 2026, hip exo, MATD3 CTDE) and SMAT/UniExo (shared-critic PPO) already use it. Publishable novelty has to come from mechanism isolation at matched budget and from partner transfer, not from the two-agent formulation.
occupied_claims: Human and assistive device as two cooperating RL agents with one critic on a shared cost in biomechanical simulation: Wu et al., NeurIPS 2022 (knee prosthesis, OpenSim, doi 10.52202/068431-1980). Human plus hip exoskeleton as heterogeneous MARL agents with a CTDE critic: Sun et al., Med Biol Eng Comput 2026 (doi 10.1007/s11517-026-03634-9). Staged or shared-critic PPO co-adaptation of a musculoskeletal human and a hip exoskeleton, with hardware results: SMAT (2603.07618, 2608.00715) and UniExo (2609.19690).

Sequential one-agent-at-a-time updates converge where simultaneous independent updates may not, and multi-timescale PPO interpolates between them: Nekoei et al., CoLLAs 2023 (2302.02792). Sequential trust-region updates with a monotonic-improvement guarantee: HATRPO/HAPPO (2109.11251), HARL (2304.09870), A2PO (2302.06205).
Alternating best-response and independent updates can converge to initialisation-dependent suboptimal Nash equilibria, with an exact decentralised joint-gradient fix: ACPO, RLC 2026 (2606.30072).

Co-trained or self-play agents fail with held-out or independently trained partners, and partner-diversity training mitigates it: Carroll 2019 (1910.05789), Other-Play 2020 (2003.02979), FCP 2021 (2110.08176), MEP (2112.11701), HSP (2302.01605), COLE (2302.04831). Shown for assistive physical HRI with a withheld humanoid population: Assistax (2507.21638).
Critic centralisation is not strictly beneficial, and state-based critics can be biased: Lyu et al., AAMAS 2021 (2102.04402) and JAIR 2023 (2408.14597).

Cooperative co-adaptive MDPs with gated policy improvement and Nash-equilibrium convergence conditions for human-machine rehabilitation: Guo et al. 2023 / Knowledge-Based Systems 2024, Su et al. 2025 (2503.07319), and An et al. DAMMRL, IEEE TNNLS 2026 (doi 10.1109/tnnls.2026.3685832).
A machine's adaptation rule and rate select Nash vs Stackelberg outcomes with real humans: Chasnov et al., Scientific Reports 2025 (2305.01124).
A frozen pre-trained musculoskeletal human policy used as a fixed evaluator for co-optimising a device's structure and controller: Zuo et al. 2026 (2603.09218).
open_gaps: No paper found tests partner transfer in human-device co-adaptation (SMAT, UniExo, MBEC 2026, Wu 2022). The open test is a cross-play matrix of exo seeds against independently trained humans (varying seeds, implementations, reward shapings and impairments). Score it as the benefit retained relative to a partner-specific best response, the BR-Prox idea of ZSC-Eval (2310.05208).

No study separates the update schedule from the curricula in human-device co-adaptation. The open design crosses schedules {SMAT staging, simultaneous, simultaneous from the Stage-2 human, HAPPO order, multi-timescale ratio and switching period} with {reward curriculum on/off} x {torque curriculum on/off} at matched transitions. Each arm is cheap once throughput is solved.

Shared critic vs MAPPO-style centralised critic vs IPPO vs ACPO-style decentralised critics has not been compared in a physically coupled, strongly asymmetric pair (26 muscles vs 2 torques, exo observing an 18-D window). Lyu et al.'s bias and variance analysis gives falsifiable predictions.
Does staging change the endpoint or only the path? Restart simultaneous training from the staged endpoint and vice versa, and check whether each joint policy is a fixed point of the other schedule.
Remedy side: does training the exo FCP-style against a frozen population of SMAT human checkpoints (across stages and seeds) buy held-out transfer without losing the co-trained partner's benefit?

Prosthesis side: no 2023-2026 paper was found that trains a musculoskeletal human and a prosthesis controller as two deep-RL agents. Wu et al. 2022 used impedance parameters and 6-unit networks, and 2607.22858 (2026) replays recorded hip kinematics instead of modelling the human.
unverifiable: No seed failed verification: all 11 seeds resolved on the arXiv API on 2026-09-23 with matching titles. The MAPPO arXiv title has a comma ('Cooperative, Multi-Agent') that the NeurIPS/Crossref title (doi 10.52202/068431-1787) lacks.

Seeds verified but not selected (16-entry cap): MADDPG (1706.02275, NeurIPS 2017; CTDE origin, off-policy, covered by MAPPO and Lyu), COMA (1705.08926, AAAI 2018, doi 10.1609/aaai.v32i1.11794; counterfactual per-agent baseline, a possible exo-credit diagnostic) and Luck et al. (1911.06832, CoRL 2019; morphology-controller co-adaptation, tangential to Phase 1).
Assistax first appeared 2025-07-29 (v1). v2 (2026-06-02) and v3 (2026-07-21) are the RLC 2026 versions, so published_after_2026_04 is false.
Sun et al. (MBEC 2026): title, authors and date verified on Crossref and the Springer page, and the abstract was read. The full text is paywalled and was not read, and no code statement was seen.
Wu et al. (NeurIPS 2022): verified on the NeurIPS proceedings page and in the PDF (method and evaluation sections read). No arXiv version and no code link were found.

An et al., DAMMRL, IEEE TNNLS 2026 (doi 10.1109/tnnls.2026.3685832): title and authors from Crossref, abstract from OpenAlex. The IEEE page was blocked, so the method details are unverified. Not selected.

UniExo (2609.19690): the shared critic with one PPO update, the frozen-human predictor stage and the absence of held-out-partner evaluation were confirmed in the arXiv HTML. The code is 'to be made publicly available' and no repository was found. Not selected here because the adjacent-SOTA cluster covers it.
